title: Why the Federal Minimum Wage Feels Stuck

scenes.narration: Did you know the federal minimum wage has been frozen for over 15 years?

visual.text: Why the Federal Minimum Wage Feels Stuck

scenes.narration: Since July 2009, the federal rate has remained locked at $7.25 per hour.
While that number stayed still, inflation has continued to climb higher every single year.
This means your hard-earned dollars buy significantly less today than they did back in 2009.
The full story is on the channel.

scenes.narration: How much has average pay grown compared to the minimum wage since 1970?
Between 1970 and 2026, the federal minimum wage rose by 353%.
In that same period, average pay for non-managers skyrocketed by 889%.
The gap between the floor and the average worker has widened drastically over the decades.

title: The Silent Pay Cut of Inflation

scenes.narration: Are your wages losing the race against rising prices?

visual.text: The Silent Pay Cut of Inflation

scenes.narration: Since 1980, consumer prices have jumped by 333%.
In the same timeframe, the federal minimum wage only grew by 134%.
Without automatic adjustments, inflation turns into a silent pay cut for the lowest earners.
